title: First-order languages: terms, formulas, and substitution
summary: First-order signatures, finite terms and formulas, free variables, and substitution that keeps variable binding intact.
abstract: The assertion that every object has a larger object needs more structure than a propositional letter: it refers to objects, a relation, and a quantifier ranging over those objects. A first-order language supplies symbols for functions and relations, while its terms and formulas specify how those symbols can be combined. We distinguish free variables, whose values can be supplied from outside, from occurrences governed by a quantifier. This distinction lets us substitute terms without accidentally binding a variable, and structural induction proves that the substitution uses exactly the free variables we expect.
